opener: Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?

messages.content: You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
When iron is introduced, it gives up electrons to the copper ions in the solution. That electron transfer is the key to the colour change you see.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
The blue colour indicates Cu²⁺ ions. The iron displaces those ions, so copper metal coats the nail.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen and water, producing Fe₂O₃. In copper sulphate, iron reacts with Cu²⁺ ions instead, so you get copper metal on the nail.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
If it were merely dirt, the blue solution would remain unchanged. The colour shift shows a chemical reaction, not just contamination.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
Copper sulphate provides Cu²⁺ ions that accept electrons from iron. That electron acceptance turns the ions into solid copper on the nail.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
Yes, because only a small amount of copper is deposited on the nail, leaving most Cu²⁺ ions in solution to keep the blue hue.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
Exactly! The iron acts as the anode, losing electrons, while copper ions act as the cathode, gaining electrons and forming metal.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
Iron dissolves as Fe²⁺, but in the presence of Cu²⁺ it prefers to transfer its electrons to copper ions, so it stays solid and deposits copper instead.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
Zinc is also more reactive than copper, so it would also reduce Cu²⁺ to copper metal, leaving the zinc dissolved as Zn²⁺ in solution.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
If you stir the solution and the blue colour fades, that indicates most copper ions have been reduced. A persistent blue means some ions remain.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
Try rinsing the nail with water and then drying it. If the coating remains, it's likely copper; if it washes off, it's probably an impurity.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
Because only a small fraction of the Cu²⁺ ions are reduced. The majority stay in solution, maintaining the blue colour.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
If you add a stronger oxidising agent, like nitric acid, the deposited copper can dissolve back into the solution as Cu²⁺.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
Steel contains iron and other metals; the iron part will still reduce Cu²⁺, but the other metals might also participate, altering the reaction slightly.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
The green patina, or verdigris, forms when copper reacts with CO₂ and moisture over time. In a fresh copper sulphate solution, you’ll mainly see metallic copper, not verdigris.
You are a Socratic science tutor for Grade 10 Nepal SEE.
Why does an iron nail placed in copper sulphate solution turn coppery?
Yes, the persistence of blue indicates that not all Cu²⁺ ions have been reduced. The reaction continues until equilibrium is reached.
